# Teacher turn S0 contract

This document freezes the safety boundary for one logical Student turn. S1
adds migration `017_create_teacher_dialog_dense_turns`, durable per-dialog
cursors, proof/outcome records, fenced claims, lease renewal, and atomic
terminal completion. Dense v2 claiming remains disabled by default through
`TEACHER_DIALOG_DENSE_ORDERING_ENABLED=false`; v1 legacy jobs remain readable
and claimable.

## Identity and ordering

`source_event_id` is the stable `dialog.teacher.requested.event_id` for one
logical Student turn. A `TeacherJobTurnCorrelation` carries
`teacher_turn_sequence`, the Dialog-owned dense per-dialog sequence, plus
`dialog_id`, `canonical_student_message_id`, `student_id`,
`personal_teacher_id`, `correlation_id`, and `causation_id` at the Teacher-job
intake boundary. Where applicable it also carries `teacher_job_id`,
`action_receipt_id`, `student_command_id`, `ai_execution_id`, and
`learning_action_id`.

`correlation_id` and the Teacher-job `causation_id` are UUIDs. Dialog's v2
event carries `dialog_causation_id` (the envelope `causation_id`), which
equals the canonical Student message ID under the current Dialog contract.
It is preserved separately and is never overwritten with Teacher-job
causation. For a text turn,
`correlation_id == canonical_student_message_id`; for an action turn,
`correlation_id == action_receipt_id`. At Teacher-job intake,
`teacher_job.causation_id == source_event_id`. This rule is scoped to that
boundary: AI Prompt execution, Student commands/receipts, and the Dialog
response each define their own boundary-specific causation ID. These are
identity bindings, not one shared downstream trace field.

Eligibility is against the expected dense `teacher_turn_sequence`: turn 2 is
ineligible until turn 1 is safe. `source_message_sequence` is retained as
evidence only and never acts as the turn cursor; it may gap or differ because
other Dialog messages share that sequence. Equal source identity is a retry of
the same turn, never a new turn. Dialog request schema v1 omits dense ordering
and uses the legacy claim path; schema v2 requires the dense sequence and
shared correlation fields. A v2 job may be durably accepted out of order, but
remains unclaimable until the flag is enabled and its sequence equals the
cursor's next value.

## Cursor advancement

A cursor may advance only from one of these terminal outcomes:

- `delivered`: Dialog has confirmed the canonical idempotent
  `teacher_response_message_id`;
- `failed_no_effect`: the turn is proven to have produced no committed Student
  transition and no Teacher reply, carries a bounded failure code, and links
  a durable recoverable outcome ID plus a durable `no_effect_proof_id`
  pointing to Student receipt/absence reconciliation. An attempted
  `student_command_id` may remain as evidence; it does not prove a committed
  transition and is allowed only with the no-effect proof. Absence of a
  failure code alone is never proof.

`unknown`, `partial`, and `committed_unreconciled` are reconciliation states,
not terminal outcomes. They block advancement and must not be converted to
success by timeout, process restart, or a best-effort retry. An accepted
Student command alone never advances the cursor; a confirmed Teacher reply is
still required.

## Trusted action boundary

The action path is one bounded provenance chain (not one shared causation
field across every service boundary):

`source prompt message/version + assistant-ui digest` → `action receipt` →
`canonical Student message` → `source_event_id` → `teacher_job_id` →
`teacher_response_message_id`.

`TeacherActionReceiptEvidence` validates the receipt ID, source prompt ID and
version, opaque `block_id`/`action_id` (ASCII, at most 128 bytes), and the
lowercase 64-character SHA-256 `source_ui_digest` before the action turn is
accepted. The evidence is only a binding and audit proof; it never grants the
LLM or Teacher direct Student mutation authority. A text turn has no receipt
boundary and starts at its canonical Student message.

## Effects and retries

One logical turn can have at most one accepted Student command. Repeating the
same `student_command_id` is a replay; a different command key is an integrity
conflict. The Teacher reply uses one deterministic Dialog command key and
`teacher_job_id`. A retry may replay the same committed message, but may not
append a second message or replace its message identity.

Student remains the owner of Student state. LLM output is a bounded draft only;
it cannot contain or execute a Student mutation. All model execution crosses
the AI Prompt boundary; Teacher does not call a provider directly.

For product-aware onboarding v2, an accepted Student effect is not terminal.
Teacher proves the receipt, reads state-fenced Planner readiness, and atomically
stages the deterministic response before Dialog delivery. A stale, invalid, or
unavailable read cannot become `failed_no_effect` or advance the cursor.
Recovery from `student_staged` repeats the receipt proof; `no_effect`, tangent,
and response-staged paths make zero readiness calls. Durable accepted+no-UI
delivery closes its prompt, while a tangent/no-effect no-UI delivery preserves
it across crash retry.

## Observability boundary

Reserved low-cardinality metric dimensions are limited to bounded categories
such as `outcome`, `reconciliation_state`, `boundary`, and `context_type`.
IDs (`action_receipt_id`, `source_event_id`, `teacher_job_id`,
`teacher_response_message_id`, `canonical_student_message_id`, and
`ai_execution_id`) may appear in structured logs for correlation, but must not
be metric labels. S1 adds no observability subsystem or collector; worker
concurrency is bounded by `TEACHER_DIALOG_WORKER_CONCURRENCY`.

The domain value objects and executable invariants are in
`internal/domain/teacher_turn_contract.go` and
`internal/domain/teacher_dialog_turn.go`; persistence is owned by
`TeacherDialogJobRepository` and migration 017. Retry and lease expiry never
advance the cursor. Only delivered or proof-backed failed-no-effect outcomes
can advance it; unknown, partial, and committed-unreconciled states remain
blocked.

Legacy schema-v1 completion keeps its original status, response, and
`delivered_message_id` path and does not create a dense-turn outcome record.
The additive terminal ledger and `teacher_response_message_id` are written
only for schema-v2 jobs.

## Rollout order and readiness

Migration 017 and the v2-capable Teacher binary are deployed first with
`TEACHER_DIALOG_DENSE_ORDERING_ENABLED=false`. Readiness for the next stage is
the protected Teacher readiness check plus an operator-visible capability
signal that migration 017 is present and the binary reports v2 dual-read
support; this signal is a bounded category, never an ID or metric label.
Only after that check passes is dense claiming enabled in Teacher. Dialog may
publish schema-v2 requests only after legacy queued work has drained and the
Teacher consumer is observed claiming v2. These are independent producer and
consumer switches, not one cross-service atomic flag. Rollback disables the
Dialog v2 producer first, then disables Teacher dense claiming; the schema and
v2 reader remain installed until all v2 rows are reconciled.

The protected `GET /internal/readyz` also performs a read-only backlog check.
If dense claiming is disabled and a schema-v2 job remains `queued`,
`processing`, `delivery_pending`, or `blocked`, readiness returns HTTP 503
with `status: not ready` and the static
`error_code: dense_teacher_ordering_disabled_with_pending_v2`. This includes
unresolved `unknown`, `partial`, and `committed_unreconciled` work. The check
does not change jobs, response bodies, proofs, outcomes, or cursors. Terminal
`delivered` and proof-backed `completed` history does not make readiness fail.
Dependency or missing-schema failures remain fail-closed and never expose raw
errors, identities, tokens, counts, or private response text.

| Dialog v2 producer | Teacher dense claiming | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Disabled | Disabled | Schema-v1 intake and legacy claims continue. |
| Disabled | Enabled | Schema-v1 intake and legacy claims continue. |
| Enabled | Disabled | Schema-v2 intake and duplicate ACK remain durable; V2 is not claimed and pending V2 makes protected readiness return the bounded 503 above. |
| Enabled | Enabled | Schema-v2 claims follow the existing dense cursor. |

After correcting the deployed consumer configuration, reconstructed workers
resume eligible accepted V2 work under the existing lease, retry, and cursor
rules. Readiness never auto-enables a flag or terminates valid V2 intake.
Operators must deploy uniform producer configuration and enforce the existing
legacy drain barrier across a mixed fleet; these independent switches do not
provide a distributed configuration lock. An unresolved poisoned turn remains
blocked. This diagnostic grants no timeout skip, requeue, unblock, or new
no-effect proof policy.
